messages.subject: creating cdf files
parts:
Hi,
I am starting to make a function that takes Affy's annotation file for
the exon arrays and automatically make a cdf for the core, extended
and full like Ken did previously. I read on the help file for
readCdf() that there will probably be changes for the structure of the
files for cdfs. Is there anything I should do to make this function
(somewhat) robust to these changes? Or I'll just have to fix it when
the decisions are finalized?
Best,
Elizabeth

Thanks,
Elizabeth

To be honest, I'm not sure what will be the most stable from the Affy
side of things, but the pgf and clf files are part of the 'library
files' for all the recent chips:

http://www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/libraryfilesmain.affx

I believe the pgf and clf files are used in the affymetrix software
(exon and expression analysis).

Either way, they should contain the same info.

For the Ensembl CDFs, I used the .probe.tab files from:

http://www.affymetrix.com/analysis/downloads/na23/wtexon/

Mark

parts:
On Oct 19, 5:34 pm, epurdom <epur...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Henrik and all,
>
> I have a continuing question that I hope is not too affxparser
> related. But I'm not clear about the qc parts of the cdf. Ken just
> didn't define any qc elements and neither did the affy cdf he was
> starting with. But I have that information, so I would like to include
> it (This should be incorporated for the background correction, since
> there are specific background correction control probes to take the
> place of MM.).
>
> All I find is that the the 'cdfqc' part of writecdf is 'A list with
> one component for each QC unit'; is it the same kind of list structure
> as cdf, but only the qc units? And should the probes in the cdf and
> cdfqc parts be exclusive, or is cdfqc a subset of cdf?
>
> And then what happens to those qc elements? Do they get automatically
> cut out of functions like fitting the genelevel models, etc.?

Hi Elizabeth

Affxparser uses the same terminology as Affy for the probesets. What
we (they) call QC units is _not_ what you are thinking of (I am 100%
sure). QC units in a CDF file is special probesets that
1) do not have a name
2) do not have a block/group structure
The QC units are typically not being read by any software that reads
CDF files (except readCdfQcUnits). They consists of special probes
that are (amongst other stuff) used for gridding of the image: if you
have ever looked at a high-resolution imgae plot you will have noted
that there is a checkerboard pattern along the edge of the chip + also
a chip name embedded in the image. These pixels are coming from QC
probes.

It might be interesting to look at "QC" probes from a statistical QC
perspective, but no-one has done so and their presence is not being
used by any software I know of.

In addition to the QC units Affy also provides (at least on some
chips), units with names such as "AFFX-BioD". These probesets
(depending on the chip and experimental protocol) are more along what
I would think of as quality control probesets: they target special
genes that are added to the hybridization mix and the distribution of
intensities could be considered a proxy for the quality of the chip.
Just the fact that these probesets have names tell us they are not
"QC" units from a tecnhnical Affy CDF file lingo point of view.

So in short , on a normal Affy chip (let us just think gene expression
here) you have qc units (not used by anyone, probably not relevant in
any analysis), special affy probesets with names and "normal"
probesets targeting something.

For Exon arrays I am pretty sure that one of the reasons Ken did not
include QC probesets was the fact that since the chip is so big, some
of the QC probesets were gigantic with 1000's or more probes. These
probesets were problematic due to their size, so I assume Ken just
opted for an exclusion - an easy decision since they are not being
used by anybody.

As stated above, QC units are not being read by almost any software.
Even using affxparser/aroma.affymetrix you need to do special stuff to
access them.

Kasper
